transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Halo Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Halo Platform), Evelyn Smith (Halo CTO), Jared Kim (Halo SRE)

Summary: quick discovery focused on integration paths for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for realtime chat assistants and batch embedding jobs. Key topics: SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain / LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy patterns (internal API gateway vs Redwood gateway), rate limits & quota model, observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost), compliance questions (SOC2, KMS).

Topics:
- Integration options and recommended SDKs
- LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters and caching strategies
- Gateway/proxy architecture and deployment patterns
- Rate limiting, quotas, and throttling behavior
- Observability hooks and traceability for prompts and tokens

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're on for 45ish minutes; quick intros then we'll jump into how you'd like to integrate with Redwood and what constraints you have.
[00:18] Maya: hi, Maya here, Head of ML at Halo, we run chat assistants for customer support and also nightly embedding jobs for search. main things for us are latency for chat and cost for embeddings.
[00:32] Carlos: Carlos platform eng, we'll own the infra side; our concerns are VPC peering, proxying traffic through our gateway, and RBAC/SSO.
[00:45] Sophie: great; Liam is our SE and will do the deep technical Qs. Liam?
[00:51] Liam: Hey team; first, what's your target p99 latency for chat and what throughput do you expect?
[01:02] Maya: p99 we'd like under 400ms for single-turn, average load ~200 qps during peak for chat, embeddings are batched overnight ~10k docs per day.
[01:18] Liam: ok cool, that guides whether hosted can meet SLA or you need Dedicated. Hosted often handles that for a lot of customers but dedicated gives pinned GPU pools and consistent latency.
[01:31] Evelyn: can you explain differences for us? specifically around data isolation and network flow.
[01:37] Sophie: yes — hosted is our SaaS API, data retention configurable but processed in multi-tenant infra; dedicated is reserved capacity with isolated GPU pools and optional VPC peering; private is full control, can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem. Data residency + KMS integrations are available for dedicated/private.
[01:58] Jared: for us, SSO and audit logs are musts. Do you expose audit events and per-request tracing?
[02:05] Liam: we surface token-level cost, per-request latency, and you can ship traces to your tracing backend via our tracing hooks (OTel compatible), also audit logs to S3 or your logging endpoint.
[02:18] Maya: nice — on the SDK side, what language support and do you have first-class LangChain or LlamaIndex connectors?
[02:27] Liam: we have official Python and Node SDKs; we also maintain sample adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. the LangChain adapter handles streaming and tool-calls, and there are recipes for prefix caching and KV cache integration.
[02:44] Carlos: is the LangChain adapter maintained by Redwood or community? we use LlamaIndex heavily and want low-friction.
[02:51] Liam: Redwood-maintained examples, plus a pattern for LlamaIndex that uses Redwood's embeddings endpoint; we'll share a repo with examples. some bits are community PRs but core adapters we support.
[03:05] Maya: how does caching work — KV cache, prefix caching? we sometimes have repeated prompts so want to reduce tokens.
[03:13] Liam: we do prefix/KV caching at the gateway level for hosted and can enable it inside dedicated runtime as well; caching policies are workload-aware. note: KV cache is sometimes transcribed as KV cash in our docs—ha, but it is cache.
[03:29] Sophie: another pattern is to run a small Redis instance in front of your app to dedupe prompts; we can show how batching + prefix caching interacts.
[03:38] Carlos: about the gateway/proxy: do you recommend sending traffic direct to Redwood or routing through our internal gateway?
[03:45] Liam: both patterns are supported. direct to Redwood is simpler (for hosted) and minimizes your maintenance. proxying through your gateway is common for customers that want additional auth, request masking, or to add rate-limiting rules. with proxying you'll want to be careful about streaming — keep the connection open and proxy supports chunked transfer.
[04:05] Maya: for streaming, any gotchas with WebSockets vs HTTP/2 vs SSE?
[04:10] Liam: we support streaming via chunked HTTP responses and SSE for browser clients; WebSocket is common in our dedicated setups but it's essentially a transport choice. we'll share best-practices doc.
[04:23] Jared: rate limits — if we hit a burst above commit on Dedicated, how does fallback happen? do you automatically spill to hosted?
[04:32] Sophie: we have routing policies: you can prefer dedicated, then fallback to hosted or a lower-cost model. but automatic spillover requires a configured fallback policy and compatibility between model variants.
[04:44] Evelyn: what about quotas and billing spikes — how granular are quotas?
[04:49] Liam: quotas can be per-api-key, per-route, per-organization. billing spikes are tracked; you can set hard caps or soft alerts. for dedicated pricing we typically have commit bands and burst capacity options.
[05:02] Maya: observability — can we tag requests with our internal request_id and get token-level breakdowns correlated?
[05:09] Liam: yes, you can pass metadata headers (x-halo-request-id) and it'll be present in logs/trace correlations in the console and exported via our tracing hooks.
[05:19] Carlos: how about latency breakdown — tokenization, model forward, network?
[05:24] Liam: we provide per-token timing, model-inference time, and transport time in the console; for deeper dives we can send detailed traces with spans to your OTel collector.
[05:35] Maya: great — on the SDK examples, do you have a LangChain Chains example that shows reranking + embeddings pipeline?
[05:44] Liam: yes, we'll include a LangChain pipeline mixing our embeddings for search and a reranker model; LlamaIndex patterns for indexing and query-time retriever are also in the repo.
[05:56] Sophie: want to talk about security briefly — KMS support, bring-your-own-key?
[06:02] Evelyn: yes, BYOK is critical.
[06:05] Liam: we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via PKCS11 in private). with Dedicated and Private you can opt into customer-managed keys so Redwood doesn't have plaintext access to model inputs in storage buckets.
[06:20] Maya: any certification posture — SOC 2, ISO?
[06:23] Sophie: SOC 2 Type II in scope; we have documentation and controls. we'll attach the compliance pack.
[06:30] Carlos: deployment-wise, if we go private in our VPC, how are updates handled? we prefer controlled rollouts and ability to pin runtime versions.
[06:38] Liam: private is delivered as a customer-controlled control plane with an agent; you can pin model versions, approve rollouts, and we support canary and A/B strategies for model changes.
[06:48] Maya: latency targets — if we need <250ms p99 will we definitely need dedicated or private?
[06:55] Liam: depends on your sequence lengths and model choice. for shorter prompts and efficient backbones hosted might be fine. for sub-250ms p99 at scale, pinned dedicated pools or colocating inference near your users is common.
[07:06] Sophie: want to bring up billing for embeddings — per-embedding vs bulk pricing?
[07:11] Liam: embeddings can be usage-based or included in a commit band for Dedicated; for large-volume customers we typically offer a discounted per-embedding rate in the contract.
[07:21] Maya: integration with Vector DBs — do you provide connectors or do we push embeddings to our DB?
[07:27] Liam: we provide examples for Pinecone, Milvus, and we have a simple push-to-S3 flow. most customers push embeddings into their chosen vector DB; we also support a managed vector-indexing pipeline as an add-on.
[07:38] Carlos: about quotas again — are there per-minute QPS quotas that can cause 429s? and what's retry semantics recommended?
[07:46] Liam: yes, 429s can surface if you exceed hard rate limits. we recommend exponential backoff with jitter; for critical traffic consider dedicated with higher commit.
[07:56] Jared: do you expose a local gateway or sidecar pattern for private? we want minimal changes to our service mesh.
[08:03] Liam: for private we have a sidecar/agent pattern and a gateway that can be deployed inside your service mesh. that said many customers prefer an internal proxy that routes to Redwood endpoints — both supported.
[08:13] Sophie: I'll share an example manifest for the sidecar and a proxy config.
[08:18] Maya: let's talk about model compatibility — if we pick a model family, are tool-calling and structured outputs consistent?
[08:26] Liam: most modern LLMs support the primitives we expose: streaming tokens, function/tool-calls, structured JSON. some model variants differ in prompt-format sensitivity; we maintain compatibility shims.
[08:40] Maya: can you host custom fine-tuned models?
[08:44] Liam: yes, you can bring a fine-tuned artifact; for Dedicated/Private we load them into the runtime. for Hosted we support hosted custom models with vetting.
[08:55] Carlos: what's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated vs Private?
[08:59] Sophie: Dedicated is typically 4–6 weeks to provision and tune; Private can be 6–12 weeks depending on network and compliance needs.
[09:09] Maya: on the SDK side, we use LlamaIndex v0.9.x — any compatibility issues?
[09:15] Liam: we have examples for current LlamaIndex versions; sometimes helper functions move but patterns hold. we'll mark the example with tested versions.
[09:25] Sophie: are there any data residency restrictions we should be aware of?
[09:29] Liam: you can choose region for Dedicated and Private; hosted regions available in NA/EU with more coming.
[09:35] Maya: for our batch embeddings job — can we push a large bulk job via an async API and get callbacks when done?
[09:42] Liam: yes, async batch APIs are supported; you can provide a callback URL or poll job status.
[09:48] Carlos: about observability hooks — will the console show token-level cost mapped to users or routes?
[09:54] Liam: the console supports per-route and per-api-key breakdowns and you can create custom dashboards; token-level cost mapping to a user requires you to surface user_id in request metadata.
[10:05] Maya: any limitations on prompt length or max tokens we should plan for?
[10:10] Liam: max context depends on model; runtime supports long context models and we recommend streaming or chunking for very large inputs.
[10:18] Sophie: quick question from our CSM — how do we handle rate-limit notifications? email, webhook, or Slack?
[10:24] Aisha: we can configure alerts to email, webhook, or Slack channel — and also push alerts to your PagerDuty.
[10:31] Evelyn: security again — can you restrict outbound egress from the runtime for private? we need to ensure no unexpected external calls.
[10:39] Liam: private can be deployed with strict egress controls; there is an allowlist for external integrations and you can disable external access.
[10:46] Carlos: integrations — do you support our existing API gateway (Kong) or service mesh patterns?
[10:51] Liam: yes, customers use Kong, Envoy, Istio; we provide example Envoy configs and recommend keeping streaming alive and chunked.
[11:02] Maya: let's walk through a hypothetical integration flow — we have a microservice that accepts user chat, calls LlamaIndex retriever, then hits Redwood for answer generation, returns to user. any recommended middleware?
[11:17] Liam: put a caching layer before Redwood to dedupe prompts, add retries with backoff for non-idempotent calls, and attach request metadata for traceability; for chat set up session-level KV caching to preserve context and use conversation-state keys.
[11:33] Sophie: we'll attach a sample repo that wires LangChain + LlamaIndex + Redis + Redwood SDK.
[11:39] Maya: excellent. about billing visibility — can product managers see cost per feature?
[11:44] Liam: yes, the Console has per-route and tag-based cost reporting; you can tag calls with feature IDs.
[11:51] Carlos: do you support separate orgs or subaccounts for dev/staging/prod to avoid bleed?
[11:57] Sophie: yes, multi-tenant org structure with subaccounts and roles.
[12:02] Maya: hypothetical numbers — if we run 200 qps peak with avg 60 tokens per request for chat, any rough cost estimate?
[12:11] Liam: rough calc, we'll send a pricing calc but ballpark depends on model; we'll prepare an example pricing sheet for chat vs embedding with your token numbers.
[12:23] Jared: any demo or benchmark we can run ourselves?
[12:26] Sophie: we offer a guided benchmark with a short script; we can run it against dedicated pool for 1 hour.
[12:33] Maya: and what's required from us to run benchmarks?
[12:36] Liam: sample prompts (100–200), a traffic profile (qps and sequence length distribution), and a test API key. we can also do network RTT tests from your region.
[12:47] Evelyn: do you have a data processing addendum for EU customers?
[12:51] Sophie: yes we have DPA and standard contractual clauses; we'll include those in the security pack.
[12:58] Maya: any known gotchas when using LlamaIndex + streaming?
[13:02] Liam: streaming with retrievers can be tricky — you may want to precompute embeddings for heavy retriever usage and stream only the final generation tokens; we'll show a pattern.
[13:14] Carlos: how do we handle model rollbacks if a new model has a regression?
[13:19] Liam: use canary/A-B rollouts; Redwood can automatically fallback to previous model variant if quality drops or latency SLO breached.
[13:29] Sophie: I'll note that on next steps.
[13:33] Maya: question on quota enforcement — will individual SDK clients get soft throttling before hard 429s?
[13:40] Liam: yes, soft throttles with headers indicating remaining quota are supported so clients can react gracefully.
[13:47] Jared: do you provide client-side libraries that respect those headers and auto backoff?
[13:53] Liam: our SDK includes a basic retry/backoff implementation and exposes hooks for custom behavior.
[14:01] Carlos: curious about local testing — is there a mock server or sandbox for devs to iterate without cost?
[14:07] Sophie: we provide a free sandbox with reduced rates and a local mock binary for basic dev tests.
[14:16] Maya: this is all great. shall we move to wrap-up and explicit next steps?
[14:21] Sophie: yes — recap: we'll send security pack + SOC2, LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo, sidecar/gateway examples, and an initial pricing calc. Halo will share traffic profile and sample prompts; Carlos will create SSO test account. we'll also schedule the 1-hour benchmark for week of 3/23.
[14:42] Evelyn: sounds good. any objections to the timeline?
[14:46] Maya: aligns with our timeline.
[14:49] Sophie: perfect. thanks everyone.

Notes/Artifacts mentioned:
- LangChain + LlamaIndex sample repo (Redwood will share)
- Security pack (SOC2, DPA, KMS integration notes)
- Proxy/Envoy example and sidecar manifest
- Benchmark script and pricing spreadsheet

End transcript.
